sources.note: Bolts a small trainable recurrent block between a frozen 1.1B language model's body and its output head, so reasoning happens as repeated refinement of two latent vectors rather than as generated tokens.
sources.title: Think Deep, Speak Once: Relit, A Recursive Latent Implicit Transformer Framework

sources.note: Replaces the single tolerance threshold that RLVR uses to score floating-point answers with a hybrid reward pairing a hard clinical-safety constraint against a continuous precision-sensitive term, and adds a reward for stating the computational formula explicitly so an external verifier can check it.
sources.title: MedCalc-R1: Knowledge-Guided Reward Framework for Medical Mathematical Reasoning

result.definition: An OpenAI reasoning model appearing twice in this archive as a proprietary reference point that smaller trained models are measured against. In the clinical calculation work it is the baseline that a 1.5B and a 3B model surpass by a large margin on dosage calculation after knowledge-guided reward training, which is the paper's evidence that targeted reward design can substitute for scale on a narrow high-value task. In the recursive latent reasoning comparison it is one of the reasoning models listed on logic benchmarks, in a table the archive's reading flags as not like-for-like since the recursive model was trained on each dataset's training split while the language-model numbers are few-shot. Neither source describes the model.
